deep.reconstruction:
Context: folio 15v states Lagrange's series. If x = t + u X(x), with X = X(x), then for any function φ: φ(x) = φ(t) + u X φ'(t) + u^2/2! d/dt[X^2 φ'] + u^3/3! d^2/dt^2[X^3 φ'] + ..., with x = t after differentiation. That page also says the needed identities will be proved (section II). This page carries out that proof. It is the classical partial-differential-equation proof. Regard x = x(t,u) as defined implicitly by x = t + u X(x).

(a) Differentiate the defining equation partially with respect to t and to u:
 x_t = 1 + u X_t = 1 + u X'(x) x_t,
 x_u = X + u X_u = X + u X'(x) x_u.

(b) Eliminate X'(x). [Step filled in by me:] (1 - uX') x_t = 1 and (1 - uX') x_u = X. Hence
 x_u = X x_t.

(c) By the chain rule, ∂φ(x)/∂t = φ'(x) x_t and ∂φ(x)/∂u = φ'(x) x_u. (Gauss's second factor reads dx/dt; it should be dx/du.) Therefore
 ∂φ/∂u = X ∂φ/∂t ...(1).

(d) Taking φ = X (allowed, since X is a function of x) gives
 X_u = X X_t ...(2).

(e) Differentiate (1) with respect to t and with respect to u:
 φ_tu = X_t φ_t + X φ_tt ...(3),
 φ_uu = X_u φ_t + X φ_tu.

(f) Substitute (2) and (3) into the second relation:
 φ_uu = X X_t φ_t + X(X_t φ_t + X φ_tt) = 2 X X_t φ_t + X^2 φ_tt = ∂/∂t (X^2 φ_t) ...(4).

(g) Differentiating (4) with respect to u gives φ_uuu = ∂^2/∂t∂u (X^2 φ_t). The page breaks off here.

The next page continues: interchange the order of differentiation, then show ∂_u(X^n φ_t) = ∂_t(X^{n+1} φ_t) (6). Induction then gives ∂^n φ/∂u^n = ∂^{n-1}/∂t^{n-1}(X^n φ_t). At u = 0 we have x = t, so these become Lagrange's coefficients d^{n-1}/dt^{n-1}[X(t)^n φ'(t)]. Inserted into Taylor's series in u, this yields Lagrange's inversion series.
errors: In the chain-rule line Gauss writes (dφx/du) = (dφx/dx)(dx/dt). The second factor should be (dx/du); the letter appears to be overwritten in the manuscript. The conclusion (1) is nevertheless correct, because it uses x_u = X x_t.
Equation (1) and all of (1)-(4) are correct. The elimination of dX/dx tacitly assumes 1 - uX'(x) ≠ 0, i.e. that the implicit function is locally regular. This is unstated but standard.
No other errors on this page. On the following page, the citation of '(3) u. (4)' for deriving (6) should read (2) and (3). That slip is not on this page.

results.what: For x = t + uX(x): ∂x/∂u = X ∂x/∂t, and hence ∂φ(x)/∂u = X ∂φ(x)/∂t for any φ.
results.modern_name: First-order PDE characterization of the implicit function in Lagrange inversion (the key lemma of Laplace's proof)
results.usually_credited_to: Laplace (1777/1780, Mémoires de l'Académie des Sciences); standard in textbooks, e.g. Whittaker & Watson §7.32

results.what: ∂^2φ/∂u^2 = ∂/∂t (X^2 ∂φ/∂t). This is the first step of the induction ∂^nφ/∂u^n = ∂^{n-1}/∂t^{n-1}(X^n ∂φ/∂t), leading to the Lagrange series.
results.modern_name: Lagrange inversion theorem (Lagrange–Bürmann series), Laplace's proof
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1770) for the series; Laplace (1777) for this proof

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, correct student-style write-up of Laplace's well-known PDE proof of Lagrange's inversion formula. The references on the previous page (Lexell, Condorcet, Cousin, Pfaff's Archiv) suggest an early date, around 1795-1800. The page is of biographical interest as evidence of young Gauss's reading, but it contains nothing mathematically new.
